source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Diversity of Living Things
points: Living things show enormous **variety** — in size, shape, colour, habitat and habit. This variety is called **biodiversity**.
**Flora** = plant life of an area; **Fauna** = animal life of an area.
To study them, living things are **grouped/classified** by shared features.

sub: **Herbs** — short, soft, green stems (e.g. spinach, wheat).
**Shrubs** — medium, bushy, woody stems branching near the base (e.g. rose).
**Trees** — tall, hard, thick woody stems (e.g. mango, neem).
**Climbers** — weak stems needing support to climb (e.g. money plant, grapevine).
**Creepers** — weak stems that spread along the ground (e.g. pumpkin, watermelon).

sections.heading: 3. Habitats
points: A **habitat** = the surroundings where an organism lives.

points.text: **Terrestrial (land) habitats:** desert, forest, grassland, mountain, polar regions.
sub: Each has different plants and animals suited to it.

points: **Aquatic (water) habitats:** freshwater (ponds, rivers, lakes) and marine (seas, oceans).
**Biotic** components = living (plants, animals); **Abiotic** = non-living (air, water, soil, light, temperature).

sections.heading: 4. Adaptations
points: **Adaptation** = special features/habits that help an organism survive in its habitat.
**Desert:** camel (long legs, stores fat in hump, little urine); cactus (spines instead of leaves, thick stem to store water).
**Aquatic:** fish (streamlined body, gills, fins); aquatic plants have flexible stems.
**Mountain/cold:** thick fur, thick skin (e.g. yak); conical trees.
Organisms **not adapted** to a habitat cannot survive there.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Biodiversity = variety of life; Flora = plants, Fauna = animals.
Plant groups: herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers, creepers.
Climbers need support; creepers spread on the ground.
Habitats: terrestrial (desert/forest/grassland/mountain) and aquatic (freshwater/marine).
Biotic = living; Abiotic = non-living (air, water, soil, light).
Adaptation = feature helping survival (camel, cactus, fish).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Climbers** need support to climb; **creepers** spread along the ground — don't swap.
Cactus **spines are modified leaves** (reduce water loss); the thick green **stem** does photosynthesis and stores water.
**Abiotic** = non-living factors (water, air, light); **biotic** = living.
A tree has a **single thick woody stem**; a shrub branches near the base.
